sections.heading: Satya Narain Agarwal,Jaipur vs Acit Circle 5, Jaipur on 30 June, 2025
content: PER: RATHOD KAMLESH JAYANTBHAI, AM By way of present appeal, the assessee challenges the order of the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals)-02, Gurugram [ for short CIT(A) ] dated 25/03/2025 for assessment year 2015-16. The said order of the ld. CIT(A) arise as against the order dated 18.12.2017 passed under section 143(3) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 [ for short Act] by ACIT, Circle-05, Jaipur [ for short AO ].
ITA No. 565/JP/2025
Satya Narain Agarwal vs. ACIT
2. In this appeal, the assessee has raised following grounds: -

3.1 During the course of assessment proceedings it was gathered that, assessee has deposited cash amounting to Rs. 64,52,500/- saving bank account по. 1939000100722332 maintained with Punjab National Bank. In order to verify the source of cash deposit in bank account(s), assessee vide questionnaire dated 06.04.2017 was asked to furnish copy of saving bank account and to explain source of the cash deposited with documentary evidences. In response to which assessee vide written submission dated submitted as under:-

The details and documents furnished by the assessee were examined and it was noticed that, assessee has deposited/paid excess cash of Rs. 4,86,143/- then available in his cash book and accordingly ld. AO made that solitary addition and completed the assessment proceeding by way of order dated 18.12.2017.

4. Aggrieved from the order of Assessing Officer, assessee preferred an appeal before the ld. CIT(A). Apropos to the grounds so raised the relevant finding of the ld. CIT(A) is reiterated here in below: 4 ITA No. 565/JP/2025

The appellant further submitted that the advances received from the above 03 persons was returned back to these parties as the agreement of sale property with them could not be materialized. Even though nowhere in the sale agreement mentioned any reason of the cancellation of the agreement of sale of the properties as well as no mention about the total sale consideration for which sale agreement was to be made. On the basis of the above facts the A.O had not found tenable the contention of assessee. Now during the appellate proceedings, Appellant has submitted that a sum of Rs. 5,25,000/- was received in cash on various dates prior to 12.08.2014 by way of sale of immovable properties through registered sale deed. These sale proceeds have not been included in the cash book of appellant due to mistake on the part of the accountant of the Satya Narain Agrawal, however, these sale proceeds were appearing in another cash book of Shree Balaji Market.

On the basis of the above narrated facts it is proved that appellant has stated his contention in two mode. First appellant had relied upon the sale agreement during the assessment proceedings and secondly sale deed & cash book of Shree Balaji Market & S.N.Agarwal. On going through the cash book of Satyanarain Agarwal & Shree Balaji Market it is revealed that appellant has shown on 12.06.2014 in the cash book of Shree Balaji Market on the credit side payment of Rs. 1,50,000/- to S N Agarwal but the same is not showing in the cash book of Satya Narain Agarwal on debit side. Thus, on 26.06.2014 in the cash book of Shree Balaji Market two entries of Rs. 75,000/- & 2,25,000/- respectively were mentioned on credit side for payment by S.N. Agarwal, but in the cash book of Satya Narain Agarwal no entry of dated 26.06.2014 are mentioned.
ITA No. 565/JP/2025

Satya Narain Agarwal vs. ACIT Consequently, considering the above narrated facts it is clear that appellant has tried to adjust the unaccounted cash in his book of accounts by making these false and fabricated documents. No such cogent documents are produced before me by which appellant could be substantiate his contention. Hence, these grounds of appeal are dismissed.

6.4 Remaining ground of appeal is general in nature and do not require adjudication. Accordingly, this ground of appeal is rejected/dismissed. 7.0 In the result, the appeal of appellant is hereby dismissed."

5. As the assessee did not find any favour, from the appeal so filed before the ld. CIT(A), the assessee has preferred the present appeal before this Tribunal on the ground as reproduced hereinabove. To support the various grounds so raised by the ld. AR of the assessee, has filed the written submissions in respect of the various grounds raised by the assessee and the same is reproduced herein below:
Ground No. 1

The learned CIT(A) called for the remand report from the AO. The learned submitted remand report dated 31.01.2020 which is placed at paper book page no. 68 to 71. The learned AO in his remand report did not at all controvert the three main contentions of the appellant as under:-

Instead, the AO who submitted the remand report got confused about some of the cancelled agreements which was not even mentioned in the assessment order by the then AO who framed the assessment. The learned CIT(A), NFAC also got confused by the remand report and the abstract cash book and the dismissed the appeal by holding that the assessee tried to adjust the unaccounted cash by false and fabricated documents (page no. 10 of the CIT(A) order).
ITA No. 565/JP/2025

Satya Narain Agarwal vs. ACIT Being aggrieved, the appellant has preferred this appeal in order to get justice. Appellant's Humble Submissions: It is most respectfully submitted that both the lower authorities grossly erred in not properly appreciating the facts as well as the provisions of law. The appellant derives business income as partner from his partnership firms and has also developed and sold immovable properties as "Shree Balaji Market Avenue" scheme, the income from which was declared on presumptive basis under section 44AD of the Income-tax Act, 1961. Source of deposit of cash in bank account was from opening cash balance (Paper Book page no. 11 to 25) and sale of immovable properties through registered sale deeds (paper book page no. 43 to 66). Following documents are submitted herewith :-

Rs.8,00,404/- i.e. opening cash balance for the year under consideration 5 Copy of registered sale deeds of immovable properties 43 to 66 at Shree Balaji Market Avenue Scheme 6 Copy of abstract of cash book of Shree Balaji Market 26 to 42 Avenue Scheme for the year under consideration It is humbly submitted that the ld. A.O. grossly erred in making the impugned addition thereby ignoring the submissions of the appellant that the source of cash deposit in bank account is mainly from sale of immovable property which is also evident from para no. 5.1 at page no. 2 of the assessment order. The ld. A.O. further erred in making the impugned addition without making a specific query or show cause regarding short balance of cash of Rs.4,86,143/- on 12.08.2014 otherwise the appellant could have specifically explained the source of cash deposit and linked it with the sale of immovable properties. Admittedly, the appellant also erred during the assessment proceedings in properly linking the cash receipts from sale of immovable properties to the cash deposits in bank account. The short cash balance of Rs.4,86,143/- is because of the following reasons :-
ITA No. 565/JP/2025

tax return efiled for the immediately preceding assessment year 2014-15 (paper book page no. 11 to 25, relevant page no. 25). This opening balance of Rs.8,00,404/- is shown by the appellant in its two cash books (first of Mr. Satya Narain Agrawal and the second of Shree Balaji Market Scheme, the income the income of which is declared u/s 44AD ) as under :-

Hence from the above, it is amply evident that the appellant had additional cash balance to the extent of Rs.2,80,000/- in addition to Rs.5,25,000/- as sale proceeds from immovable properties (explained in detail at s.no. 2 below), total amounting to Rs.8,05,000/- which is more than sufficient to cover short cash balance computed by the ld. A.O. at Rs.4,86,143/- which was added as unexplained cash deposits.

The learned CIT(A) forwarded the Rule 46A application of the appellant (paper book page no. 67) alongwith written submissions and paper book of the appellant to the AO against which the learned AO furnished remand report dated (paper book page no. 68 to 71) but the AO didn't contradict the availability of cash to the extent of Rs.2,80,000/- from opening balance. Even the learned CIT(A) didn't consider this vital issue while dismissing the appeal instead arbitrarily concluded that the appellant gave fabricated evidence thereby ignoring that how can an income tax return of preceding assessment year e-filed on the income-tax portal be fabricated.

2. Secondly from sale proceeds of immovable properties through registered sale deeds which were not considered while working out the balance of Rs.4,86,143/- which is evident from the following documents :-

A) Rs.1,50,000/- dated 12.06.2014 (Plot No. C-12, C-13, Buyer Name : Saroj Devi) 43 to 47 B) Rs.1,50,000/- dated 12.06.2014 (Plot No. C-36, C-37, Buyer Name : Sunita Devi) C) Rs.75,000/- dated 25.06.2014 (Plot No. B-15, Buyer 48 to 52 Name : Sunil Kumar) D) Rs.75,000/- dated 25.06.2014 (Plot No. B-16, Buyer Name : Akshay Agarwal) E) Rs.75,000/- dated 02.07.2014 (Plot No. C-20, Buyer 53 to 56 Name : Kishore Kumar) Total Rs.5,25,000/- 57 to 61 62 to 66 From the above, it is amply evident that a sum of Rs.5,25,000/- was received by the appellant in cash on various dates prior to 12.08.2014 in respect of sale of immovable properties through registered sale deed. These sale proceeds have not been included in the cash book of Mr. Satya Narain Agrawal submitted to the ld. A.O. due to mistake on the part of the accountant of the appellant. These sale proceeds are however appearing in another cash book of Shree Balaji Market which has been furnished at paper book page no. 26 to 42. Even otherwise the appellant is not required to maintain books of account neither for personal transaction nor for presumptive business income u/s 44AD . Whatever the appellant has maintained is an abstract of cash book not otherwise required to maintained under law as books of account are neither required to maintained for personal transactions nor for transactions u/s 44AD .

It is further submitted that Article 265 of the Constitution of India states that "No tax shall be levied or collected except by the authority of law." Departmental authorities must not take advantage of the ignorance of the assessee and it is their duty to assist the taxpayer in every reasonable way particularly in the matter of claiming and securing reliefs. Reliance is being placed on CBDT circular No.14 of 1955 dated 11.04.1955.

As evident from the remand report, the present A.O. grossly failed in appreciating the facts as well as contentions of the appellant. He has nothing to say on the crux of the appellant's submissions with regard to opening cash balance as per preceding year income tax return filed and cash received from sale of properties 10 ITA No. 565/JP/2025 Satya Narain Agarwal vs. ACIT by way of registered sale deeds at Shree Balaji Market Avenue Scheme. The ld. A.O. in his remand report did not at all controvert the three main contentions of the appellant as under:-

Secondly, the learned CIT(A) was able to locate the reason for negative cash balance in the cash book of Satya Narain Agarwal to the extent of Rs.4,50,000/- as had the cash inflow been shown in the cash book of Satya Narain Agarwal, the cash balance could not have negative to this extent. Thirdly, in case of any doubt in the mind of learned CIT(A) in the interest of justice he could have clarified it from the appellant by giving him an opportunity of being heard instead of dismissing the appeal and sustaining the addition. Hence, the action of the learned CIT(A) is against judicial propriety and also against the principles of natural justice.
ITA No. 565/JP/2025

Satya Narain Agarwal vs. ACIT It is further submitted that the learned CIT(A), while dismissing the appeal, has arbitrarily held that the appellant has given fabricated evidence which is erroneous as the evidences in the form of opening cash balance mentioned in the preceding year income tax return e-filed on the income-tax portal cannot be fabricated. Similarly, the registered sale deeds which are registered with the Sub- registrar which is another Government Department cannot be fabricated. It is humbly submitted that both the lower authorities acted arbitrarily merely on surmises and conjectures dehors the material evidences on record. Reliance is being placed on the case of Dhakeshwari Cotton Mills Ltd. 26 ITR 775 wherein Hon'ble Supreme Court held that a suspicion remains a suspicion unless the same is established and can never take place of reality. Assessment cannot be made on guesswork without any reference to any material on record. Alternatively, it is submitted that since the appellant opted for presumptive taxation and filed its return u/s 44AD , any separate addition shall be illegal and unjustified. Reliance is being placed on the judgement of Mahendra Kumar Vs NFAC (ITAT Bangalore) ITA No. 423/Bang/2023 decided on 21.09.2023 wherein it was held that as income is estimated under section 44AD of the Income Tax Act, so addition under section 68 / 69A of the Income Tax Act is impermissible. Hon'ble ITAT, Bangalore followed the judgment of Hon'ble Punjab & Haryana High Court in the case of CIT vs. Surinder Pal Anand [2010] 192 taxmann 264. In the aforesaid circumstances and in the interest of justice, it is most respectfully requested that the impugned addition, being illegal and unjustified, may kindly be deleted and the appeal may kindly be allowed."
6. To support the contention so raised in the written submission reliance was placed on the following evidence / records / decisions:
7 Rule 46A Application dated 31st December 2019 67 8 AO Remand Report dated 31.01.2020 submitted in office of CIT Appeals on 04.02.2020 68 to 71

7. The ld. AR of the assessee in addition to the above written submission so filed vehemently argued that the assessee in this appeal challenges the only solitary addition of Rs. 4,86,143/- made by the ld. AO and sustained by the ld. CIT(A). The assessee has filed the ITR disclosing income of Rs. 35,36,580/- under the presumptive taxation and the assessee therefore not liable to maintain regular books of account. However, as the case was to verify the deposit cash deposit more then the turnover disclosed during the course of assessment proceeding based on the incorrect information and without considering the property transaction the cash book submitted wherein the ld. AO found that the as on 12.08.2014 there was negative cash of Rs. 4,86,143/- i.e. cash expended / deposit without there being receipt as alleged by the revenue based on the rough cash book filed by the assessee in the assessment proceeding. Based on that ld. AO made the addition. When the matter carried before the ld. CIT(A), the assessee filed the additional evidence and therefore, the ld. AO was provided an opportunity on those additional evidence filed by the 13 ITA No. 565/JP/2025 Satya Narain Agarwal vs. ACIT assessee. Ld. AO contended that in the assessment proceeding the assessee failed to establish the negative balance explanation and therefore, he recommended to sustain the addition. Based on that remand report ld. CIT(A) also takes a view that "the appellant has tried to adjust the unaccounted cash in his books of accounts by making these false and fabricated documents."

The assessee to counter filed an affidavit and also submitted that the how can the registered documents exactly before the cash alleged to have been considered as negative be considered as fabricated. Considering that aspect he prayed to grant the necessary relief.

8. The ld DR is heard who relied on the findings of the lower authorities and more particularly advanced the similar contentions as stated in the order of the ld. CIT(A) and that of in the remand report. Based on that ld. DR prayed to sustain the addition.

9. We have heard the rival contentions and perused the material placed on record. Vide ground no. 1 the assessee raised the solitary issue of confirming the addition of Rs. 4,86,143/- u/s 69 A of the Act as unexplained cash deposits in bank account thereby ignoring the material evidences on 14 ITA No. 565/JP/2025 Satya Narain Agarwal vs. ACIT record. The brief facts related to the issue are that revenue was in possession of the information that the assessee has deposited cash amounting to Rs. 64,52,500/- saving bank account по. 1939000100722332 maintained with Punjab National Bank and the said deposit is not sufficient to the turnover disclosed by the assessee. Thus, in order to verify the source of cash deposit in bank account(s), assessee was asked to furnish copy of saving bank account and to explain source of the cash deposited with documentary evidences the assessee submitted the deposit of cash along with the copy of the cash book. Ld. AO examined those records and copy of cash book filed. Upon examination he noticed that assessee has deposited/paid excess cash of Rs. 4,86,143/- then available in his cash book and accordingly ld. AO made that addition and considered the balance cash as explained. When the matter carried before the ld. CIT(A) assessee filed the additional evidence which was admitted and forwarded to the ld. AO for his comments based on that remand report ld. CIT(A) given his finding that the assessee has tried to adjust the unaccounted cash in his book of accounts by making these false and fabricated documents.

Before us ld. AR of the assessee argued that the assessee has filed the ITR disclosing income of Rs. 35,36,580/- under the presumptive taxation and the assessee therefore not liable to maintain regular books of 15 ITA No. 565/JP/2025 Satya Narain Agarwal vs. ACIT account. However, as the case was to verify the deposit cash deposit more then the turnover disclosed during assessment proceeding. In support of that assessee filed cash book wherein the ld. AO found that as on 12.08.2014 there was negative cash of Rs. 4,86,143/- i.e. cash expended / deposit without there being receipt as alleged by the revenue based on the rough cash book filed by the assessee in the assessment proceeding.

Based on that ld. AO made the addition. When the matter was carried before the ld. CIT(A), the assessee filed the additional evidence and therefore, the ld. AO was provided an opportunity on that additional evidence filed by the assessee. Ld. AO contended that in the assessment proceeding the assessee failed to establish the negative balance explanation and therefore, he recommended sustaining the addition. Based on that remand report ld. CIT(A) also takes a view that "the appellant has tried to adjust the unaccounted cash in his books of accounts by making these false and fabricated documents."
The assessee to counter filed an affidavit and submitted that the how can the registered documents exactly before the cash becomes negative alleged to have been considered as fabricated.

Having heard the arguments, finding of the lower authority and records in the form of submission filed before us, the bench noted that it is 16 ITA No. 565/JP/2025 Satya Narain Agarwal vs. ACIT not under dispute that the assessee has filed the ITR under presumptive taxation and thereby not suppose to maintain the regular books of account. Explaining the cash deposited the assessee submitted the cash book which was not complete as contended by the assessee and thereby the additional evidence in support of negative cash balance was filed and contended by the assessee that the property transaction cash if considered based on those registered agreement placed on record there is not negative cash balance and in fact the complete cash deposit stands explained. The bench further noted that the assessee vide his letter dated 23.11.2017 contended that he is in receipt of cash of from the following persons as an advance against the plots sold to them as per details given below, which was not considered in the cash book filed before the ld. AO and if the same is considered there is not separate addition of the negative cash balance is required to made :-
ITA No. 565/JP/2025

Satya Narain Agarwal vs. ACIT The assessee filed all those documents before the ld. CIT(A) who in turned forwarded the same to AO. These documents are registered documents and therefore, the same cannot be considered as after thought when the revenue did not controvert the contention of the assessee that the said cash was not included in the cash book filed by the assessee. Before us the assessee in furtherance to the evidence already on record also filed an affidavit wherein it was submitted that the said cash received was available and was not entered into the cash book. He also declared that the opening balance shown in the cash was also taken as incorrect and that fact was supported by the affidavit and that of the ITR of the previous placed on record. Considering both these evidence if that is corrected there is no negative balance for an amount of Rs. 4,86,143/- and therefore, we are of the considered view that since the cash generated by the assessee from those registered deed with that of the corrected opening cash on hand cannot be ignored and were not after thought. Based on these observations we see no reason to sustain that addition and thereby ground no. 1 raised by the assessee is allowed.
Ground no. 2 being general and the same is not required to be adjudicated.
ITA No. 565/JP/2025
Satya Narain Agarwal vs. ACIT In the result, the appeal of the assessee is allowed.
Order pronounced in the open court on 30/06/2025.
